sentences.text: G. Narasimha vs P. Hazarathaiah on 21 July, 2023

Author: P.Sree Sudha
Bench: P.Sree Sudha
The Honourable Smt. Justice P.Sree Sudha
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2969 of 2008
J U D G M E N T:

This Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 against the Judgment and Decree dated 09.06.2003 passed in O.P.No.1014 of 2000 passed by the learned Chairman, Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-IV Additional Chief Judge,
Hyderabad.

entities.text:
Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-IV Additional Chief Judge,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
02 . The appellant/petitioner filed O.P.No.1014 of 2000, claiming compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-
for injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 30.03.2000.
The trial Court after considering the arguments of both sides, granted compensation of Rs.86,200/-.
Aggrieved by the said Judgment, petitioner therein preferred the present appeal.
There is no dispute regarding the accident, but the quantum of the compensation is only disputed, this Court is no going into other details.
03. The petitioner himself was examined as PW1.

He also got examined Doctor as PW2 who stated that according to Ex.A2 medical legal record, petitioner sustained lacerated wound over left arm about 12 X 10 cm., exposing cut muscles extending to left elbow and fracture of left capitation and fracture of lower end.
04. As seen from the record, the petitioner is a cleaner in a lorry and he earns Rs.2,000/- per month.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, as such it is reasonable to award Rs.35,000/- for injuries.

Apart from that he is also entitled for an amount of Rs.15,000/- for pain and suffering and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities and he is also entitled for Rs.10,000/-
towards medical expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards transportation charges and Rs.5,000/- towards extra nourishment.

The petitioner might not have attended his work, atleast for a period of six months, therefore, he is also entitled for an amount of Rs.12,000/- towards loss of earnings and he is also entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges.
05.

Therefore, the appellant/petitioner is entitled for the compensation in the following terms:
1. Injuries Rs.35,000/-
2. Pain and Suffering Rs.15,000/-

3. Loss of Amenities Rs.15,000/-
4. Medical Expenses Rs.10,000/-
5. Transportation Charges Rs.10,000/-
6. Extra nourishment Rs.5,000/-
7. Loss of earnings Rs.12,000/-
8. Attendant charges Rs.10,000/-

06. In the result, the Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.86,200/- to Rs.1,12,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Twelve Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till date of realization.

Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and Respondent No.2/Insurance Company shall deposit the entire amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
On such deposit, the appellant is entitled to withdraw the said amount along with interest accrued thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
